Events.RelatedBody: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. ASP.NET Core Identity scaffolding templates use the request-supplied email instead of the account's stored email for password-reset and confirmation messages. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/Scaffolding/issues/3959 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.1 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-640 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Any supported OS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages Updating scaffolding packages/tools does not repair previously generated application code. Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc contains the affected templates. Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design is a parent package that brings in the MVC generator through a minimum-version dependency. For Design, applicability depends on the resolved MVC generator: a project that independently resolves a fixed MVC version does not become vulnerable merely because it retains an older Design reference. ### 8.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.23 | 8.0.24 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.23 | 8.0.24 ### 9.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.12 | 9.0.13 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.12 | 9.0.13 ### 10.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.2 | 10.0.3 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.2 | 10.0.3 ### Additional known affected scaffolding prereleases These are exact known affected versions, not continuous prerelease intervals. Migrate to Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.3.0 [Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet) | = 9.0.0-preview.9.24509.5 | Migrate to Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.3.0 Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet has been incorporated into Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold. Version 20.3.0 supports .NET 8, 9, 10 and 11. Install it as a .NET tool, not as a project package reference. The MVC and Design project packages use the separate fixed versions listed above; 20.3.0 is not a version of those packages. ### Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.x Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold) | >= 20.0.0-preview.1.26156.3, <= 20.1.0 | 20.3.0 The 20.x tool contains the vulnerable Identity and Blazor templates for .NET 8.0 through 11.0. ### Affected legacy prereleases The following exact versions also contain affected templates: - [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) and [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design): `11.0.0-preview.1.26156.3` and `11.0.0-preview.1.26230.3`. - [Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet): `10.0.0-rc.1.25458.5` and `10.0.0-rc.1.25468.1`. Apply the generated-code repair below to applications created with these versions. For new scaffolding, use the Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.3.0 tool, which supports .NET 8 through 11. Migrating to that tool is not an update to an MVC or Design project package reference and does not repair previously generated code. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Check both the installed scaffolding package/tool version and the code it generated. Applications generated with an affected template remain affected after the tool is updated unless their handlers are corrected. The `dotnet-aspnet-codegenerator` command loads generators from the application's dependencies. Check the project's Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design and Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc references against the versions above; updating only the command-line tool does not replace those project dependencies. For applications created with `dotnet new`, check the selected SDK with `dotnet --version` in the working directory. Use `dotnet new list` to identify available templates and `dotnet new uninstall` without arguments to list separately installed template packages. Web ProjectTemplates can be bundled with an SDK or installed separately; a project package reference alone does not identify which template generated the application. ### How do I fix the issue? Update affected scaffolding packages/tools and project dependencies to the patched versions above before generating additional code. Updating scaffolding packages/tools does not repair previously generated applications. Change generated ForgotPassword and ResendEmailConfirmation handlers, including Blazor equivalents, to send only to the stored email returned for the located user; reject missing stored addresses, rebuild and redeploy affected apps. For an existing global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold installation, update the tool: ```shell dotnet tool update --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold --version 20.3.0 ``` For Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet installations, uninstall the old tool and install its replacement: ```shell dotnet tool uninstall --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet dotnet tool install --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold --version 20.3.0 ``` For a new installation, use the install command alone. For local tools, use `--local` instead of `--global` and run the commands from the directory containing the tool manifest. Visual Studio installs and uses the updated scaffolding tool automatically; command-line installations must be updated separately. Visual Studio 17.14 uses the legacy CodeGeneration packages listed above; keep Visual Studio updated and check independently maintained project dependencies. For SDK-bundled templates, install and select an updated SDK that includes the corrected ProjectTemplates version; check `global.json` if an older SDK remains selected. Update separately installed template packs independently. Updating the SDK does not necessarily replace a separately installed template pack. For the affected legacy prereleases, correct the generated handlers before using or deploying the generated application. #### Manual repair for generated Identity handlers This repair also applies to applications generated with the affected 11.0 scaffolding packages and Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet 10.0 RC versions above; it does not require migrating to a different scaffolding tool. In the generated `ForgotPassword` and `ResendEmailConfirmation` handlers, retain the existing user lookup, missing-user responses, password-reset confirmation checks, token generation and callback-URL encoding. After those user checks, retrieve the email from the located account before sending: ```csharp var storedEmail = await UserManager.GetEmailAsync(user); if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(storedEmail)) { throw new InvalidOperationException("Users must have an email."); } ``` In Razor Pages handlers, use `_userManager` instead of `UserManager`. Replace only the recipient argument `Input.Email` with `storedEmail` in `_emailSender.SendEmailAsync`, `EmailSender.SendPasswordResetLinkAsync` and `EmailSender.SendConfirmationLinkAsync`, as applicable. Keep `Input.Email` for the account lookup; do not use it as the message recipient. Apply the change to both handlers, including their Blazor equivalents, then rebuild and redeploy. Reapply the repair if affected templates generate the handlers again. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/Scaffolding. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-118741](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-118741) ### Acknowledgements - [Leonardo Souza](https://www.linkedin.com/in/capleonardo-souza) with [Delfia](https://delfia.tech/) - Attila.Cs(zerodaybugs.com) with https://zerodaybugs.com/ ### Revisions V1.0 (November 10, 2026): Advisory published.

Check both the installed scaffolding package/tool version and the code it generated. Applications generated with an affected template remain affected after the tool is updated unless their handlers are corrected. The `dotnet-aspnet-codegenerator` command loads generators from the application's dependencies. Check the project's Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design and Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc references against the versions above; updating only the command-line tool does not replace those project dependencies. For applications created with `dotnet new`, check the selected SDK with `dotnet --version` in the working directory. Use `dotnet new list` to identify available templates and `dotnet new uninstall` without arguments to list separately installed template packages. Web ProjectTemplates can be bundled with an SDK or installed separately; a project package reference alone does not identify which template generated the application. ### How do I fix the issue? Update affected scaffolding packages/tools and project dependencies to the patched versions above before generating additional code. Updating scaffolding packages/tools does not repair previously generated applications. Change generated ForgotPassword and ResendEmailConfirmation handlers, including Blazor equivalents, to send only to the stored email returned for the located user; reject missing stored addresses, rebuild and redeploy affected apps. For an existing global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold installation, update the tool: ```shell dotnet tool update --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold --version 20.3.0 ``` For Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet installations, uninstall the old tool and install its replacement: ```shell dotnet tool uninstall --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet dotnet tool install --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold --version 20.3.0 ``` For a new installation, use the install command alone. For local tools, use `--local` instead of `--global` and run the commands from the directory containing the tool manifest. Visual Studio installs and uses the updated scaffolding tool automatically; command-line installations must be updated separately. Visual Studio 17.14 uses the legacy CodeGeneration packages listed above; keep Visual Studio updated and check independently maintained project dependencies. For SDK-bundled templates, install and select an updated SDK that includes the corrected ProjectTemplates version; check `global.json` if an older SDK remains selected. Update separately installed template packs independently. Updating the SDK does not necessarily replace a separately installed template pack. For the affected legacy prereleases, correct the generated handlers before using or deploying the generated application. #### Manual repair for generated Identity handlers This repair also applies to applications generated with the affected 11.0 scaffolding packages and Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet 10.0 RC versions above; it does not require migrating to a different scaffolding tool. In the generated `ForgotPassword` and `ResendEmailConfirmation` handlers, retain the existing user lookup, missing-user responses, password-reset confirmation checks, token generation and callback-URL encoding. After those user checks, retrieve the email from the located account before sending: ```csharp var storedEmail = await UserManager.GetEmailAsync(user); if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(storedEmail)) { throw new InvalidOperationException("Users must have an email."); } ``` In Razor Pages handlers, use `_userManager` instead of `UserManager`. Replace only the recipient argument `Input.Email` with `storedEmail` in `_emailSender.SendEmailAsync`, `EmailSender.SendPasswordResetLinkAsync` and `EmailSender.SendConfirmationLinkAsync`, as applicable. Keep `Input.Email` for the account lookup; do not use it as the message recipient. Apply the change to both handlers, including their Blazor equivalents, then rebuild and redeploy. Reapply the repair if affected templates generate the handlers again. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). The `dotnet-aspnet-codegenerator` command loads generators from the application's dependencies. Check the project's Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design and Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc references against the versions above; updating only the command-line tool does not replace those project dependencies. Use `dotnet new list` to identify available templates and `dotnet new uninstall` without arguments to list separately installed template packages. For an existing global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold installation, update the tool: ```shell dotnet tool update --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold --version 20.3.0 ``` For Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet installations, uninstall the old tool and install its replacement: ```shell dotnet tool uninstall --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet dotnet tool install --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold --version 20.3.0 ``` For a new installation, use the install command alone. For local tools, use `--local` instead of `--global` and run the commands from the directory containing the tool manifest. Visual Studio installs and uses the updated scaffolding tool automatically; command-line installations must be updated separately. Visual Studio 17.14 uses the legacy CodeGeneration packages listed above; keep Visual Studio updated and check independently maintained project dependencies. For SDK-bundled templates, install and select an updated SDK that includes the corrected ProjectTemplates version; check `global.json` if an older SDK remains selected. Update separately installed template packs independently. Updating the SDK does not necessarily replace a separately installed template pack. After those user checks, retrieve the email from the located account before sending: ```csharp var storedEmail = await UserManager.GetEmailAsync(user); if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(storedEmail)) { throw new InvalidOperationException("Users must have an email."); } ``` In Razor Pages handlers, use `_userManager` instead of `UserManager`. Replace only the recipient argument `Input.Email` with `storedEmail` in `_emailSender.SendEmailAsync`, `EmailSender.SendPasswordResetLinkAsync` and `EmailSender.SendConfirmationLinkAsync`, as applicable. Keep `Input.Email` for the account lookup; do not use it as the message recipient. Apply the change to both handlers, including their Blazor equivalents, then rebuild and redeploy. Reapply the repair if affected templates generate the handlers again. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Events.RelatedBody: > **Announcement consolidated:** See the [November 2026 .NET Runtime security announcement](https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/498) and [shared feedback thread](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/137280). This original CVE post is retained for existing links. Closing it does not withdraw the advisory or its remediation guidance. ## Executive Summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Crafted PDB line metadata can exceed the caller-provided buffer and cause a heap out-of-bounds write. ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.8 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-122 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows - **Architectures:** x86, x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages On Windows x86, x64, and Arm64, Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native versions earlier than 18.9.1-beta1.26515.1 are affected when reading crafted native PDBs. ### .NET on Windows Product | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- .NET 8.0 installed on Windows | >= 8.0.0, < 8.0.34 | 8.0.34 .NET 9.0 installed on Windows | >= 9.0.0, < 9.0.23 | 9.0.23 .NET 10.0 installed on Windows | >= 10.0.0, < 10.0.15 | 10.0.15 .NET 11.0 installed on Windows | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0 | 11.0.0 ### Windows self-contained runtime packs These runtime packs deliver the .NET runtime for Windows self-contained applications. Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x86](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x86) | >= 8.0.0, < 8.0.34 | 8.0.34 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x64) | >= 8.0.0, < 8.0.34 | 8.0.34 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64) | >= 8.0.0, < 8.0.34 | 8.0.34 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x86](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x86) | >= 9.0.0, < 9.0.23 | 9.0.23 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x64) | >= 9.0.0, < 9.0.23 | 9.0.23 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64) | >= 9.0.0, < 9.0.23 | 9.0.23 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x86](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x86) | >= 10.0.0, < 10.0.15 | 10.0.15 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x64) | >= 10.0.0, < 10.0.15 | 10.0.15 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64) | >= 10.0.0, < 10.0.15 | 10.0.15 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x86](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x86) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0 | 11.0.0 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0 | 11.0.0 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0 | 11.0.0 ### Windows SDK distributions These Windows SDK distributions are affected through their bundled .NET runtime. Product | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- .NET SDK 8.0.1xx | >= 8.0.100-0, < 8.0.134 | 8.0.134 .NET SDK 8.0.4xx | >= 8.0.400-0, < 8.0.428 | 8.0.428 .NET SDK 9.0.1xx | >= 9.0.100-0, < 9.0.124 | 9.0.124 .NET SDK 9.0.3xx | >= 9.0.300-0, < 9.0.321 | 9.0.321 .NET SDK 10.0.1xx | >= 10.0.100-0, < 10.0.115 | 10.0.115 .NET SDK 10.0.4xx | >= 10.0.400-0, < 10.0.404 | 10.0.404 .NET SDK 11.0.1xx | >= 11.0.100-preview.1, < 11.0.100 | 11.0.100 ### Windows SDK updates Update each installed SDK feature band to the following version or later: - .NET SDK 8.0.1xx: 8.0.134 - .NET SDK 8.0.4xx: 8.0.428 - .NET SDK 9.0.1xx: 9.0.124 - .NET SDK 9.0.3xx: 9.0.321 - .NET SDK 10.0.1xx: 10.0.115 - .NET SDK 10.0.4xx: 10.0.404 - .NET SDK 11.0.1xx: 11.0.100 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Applications using Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native versions earlier than 18.9.1-beta1.26515.1 on Windows x86, x64, and Arm64 to read crafted native PDBs are exposed. See [affected packages](#affected-packages) for the affected .NET products on Windows. ### How do I fix the issue? Update affected .NET installations and each installed SDK feature band to the versions listed above or later. If an SDK was installed through Visual Studio, update Visual Studio as well. Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native is delivered through .NET Core rather than as a standalone customer NuGet update. For applications that deploy their own affected .NET runtime, including self-contained applications, update the runtime used to build the application, rebuild, and redeploy. Updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace an application's embedded runtime. Restart processes that have loaded the affected native reader. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/137280 ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Applications using server-side Negotiate authentication with `PolicyEnforcement.Always` are affected when their runtime package version is in the platform-specific ranges above. On Linux, this includes .NET 11 previews 1 through 6 and release candidates 1 through 3. On macOS, this includes .NET 11 previews 1 through 6. Preview 7 is not affected on either platform, and macOS release candidates 1 through 3 are not affected. Self-contained applications include their own runtime; updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace it. ### How do I fix the issue? For affected Linux and macOS .NET 11 prereleases, install .NET 11.0.0 or update each independently referenced runtime package to 11.0.0. Restart applications. Rebuild and redeploy self-contained applications; updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace their embedded runtime. An SDK update alone does not update an application's standalone package references. On macOS, `PolicyEnforcement.Always` remains unsupported and throws `PlatformNotSupportedException`. Razor can bind a component from a referenced assembly, but the generated C# can resolve a different type with the same name in the current project.

For example, a referenced library contains a component:

```csharp
namespace Library;

public class Button : Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.ComponentBase { }
```

The app contains a different, non-component type with the same name:

```csharp
namespace Library;

public class Button { }
```

And an app component imports the library's namespace:

```razor
@using Library

<Button />
```

Razor finds the referenced component and generates:

```csharp
__builder.OpenComponent<global::Library.Button>(0);
```

C# resolves `global::Library.Button` to the app's type, so the generated code fails with `CS0311` because that type isn't a component. There can also be a `CS0436` warning about the conflicting types. `global::` identifies the root namespace, not an assembly.

With the component alias support in [dotnet/roslyn#86372](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/86372), both of these have the same problem:

```razor
@using B = global::Library.Button

<B />
```

```razor
@using UI = global::Library

<UI.Button />
```

For the type alias, C# resolves `B` to the app's class, but Razor matches the library's component by name. The alias target map also compares equal when the alias changes from the library's component to the app's class, so incremental generation may not notice the change.

Razor shouldn't generate a component call that resolves to a different type from the one it bound.

I reproduced the three cases with the current compiler using a matching component descriptor. The ordinary-import path appears to predate the alias PR based on the old source, but I haven't run the example against the old compiler itself.

Issues.Title: [release/3.1] Reset current_no_gc_region_info after leaving no gc region implicitly
Issues.Body:
Backport https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/73602.

## Customer Impact
Customers reported occasional `System.InvalidOperationException` with message `The NoGCRegion mode was already in progress` when calling `GC.TryStartNoGCRegion`. This is preventing them from using this optimization and impacting their cold start latencies.

## Testing
Customers have tried the fix on .NET 6 overnight and reported the exception never appears again. Meanwhile, there is an unpatched machine and observed 72 exceptions of the same type in the same time interval, proving this does fix the bug.

## Risk
Low. This only impact customer using `TryStartNoGCRegion`, and this is the right thing to do.

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/cli) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/cli) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs
Issues.Body:
I'm completely perplexed.

I created a .Net Standard 2.0 library project.

I explicity added an AssemblyInfo.cs file, we need this because we use this utility to "stamp" our assemblies when we build them:

https://github.com/ygoe/NetRevisionTool

That utility is run as a pre/post build event and temporarily replaces placeholders in the AssemblyInformationalVersion attribute with runtime values (like repo folder name, commit ID, branch etc etc).

The completed assembly then has this info "burned" into it as we go forward.

.Net Standard is not working with this.

1. It seems to populatethe Package Version (in the project's Package section) with whatever we put into AssemblyInfo.cs for AssemblyInformationalVersion.
2. The version of the generated nuget package is always set as 1.0.0.

This is just mind blowing, is there no way we can do this seemingly simple operation any more if adopt .Net Standard?

Issues.Title: Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions
Issues.Body:
I was looking through this repository to determine if .NET Standard 2.1 libraries support default interface methods - it looks like they do, given the presence of `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RuntimeFeature.DefaultImplementationsOfInterfaces`, as well as my own experimenting in VS 2019. It seems I was mistaken when thinking that this was not the case, so I'm glad this repository is easily accessible to determine this.

But while doing this, I found it difficult to determine what commits were included in this particular .NET Standard version. I see that there's a tag `v2.1.0-prerelease.19126.1`, as well as branches `release/2.0.0`, `release/3.0`, and `release/3.0-preview9`. One of the machines I tested VS 2019 on had a `netstandard.dll` assembly, itself targeting .NETStandard v2.1.0, with AssemblyInformationalVersion `1.1.0+a5b5f2e1e369972c8ff1e2183979fab6099f52ef`; this commit is part of the `release/3.0` branch. However, another machine had a same-named assembly, targeting .NETCoreApp v3.0 and AssemblyInformationalVersion `3.0.0+4ac4c0367003fe3973a3648eb0715ddb0e3bbcea`, and I don't see that commit hash in this repository.

Additionally, [this blog post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/the-future-of-net-standard/) states that 2.1 will be the last version, but there is another prerelease tag `v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1` and [on GitHub](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/releases/tag/v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1) it's labelled .NET 5.0 Preview 2.

So I have a few questions for understanding this repository:

1. Since .NET Standard 2.1 is released, are there plans to continue development in this repository for e.g. the shared BCL going forward with .NET 5+?
2. Are there multiple kinds of `netstandard.dll` for a single .NET Standard version? E.g. are there separate versions for .NET Framework to reference and for .NET Core / .NET 5+ to reference?
3. Do the tags / branch names in this repository correspond to a .NET Standard version or something else?
4. It looks like there are patch releases; are there patch versions of a single .NET Standard version?
5. Are there other repositories which are being used to create `netstandard.dll`?
6. Is there a way to determine, from the repository, which commit is the one used for a given release?

Thank you for your consideration.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions" (#1777)

Issues.Title: Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1
Issues.Body:
# Summary

.NET Standard version is not resolved correctly when a transitive dependency targets multiple .NET Standard versions.

# Environment

- Windows 10 (19042.746)
- .NET 5 SDK 5.0.201

# Minimal reproducible example
[bug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/files/6209239/bug.zip)

This is a three-project solution:
- `TestProject1` targeting `netcoreapp3.1`
- `ClassProject1` targeting `netstandard2.0`
- `ClassProject2` targeting *both* `netstandard2.0` and `netstandard2.1`

The project dependency chain is: `TestProject1 -> ClassProject1 -> ClassProject2`

A method (`ClassProject2Test1`) on `ClassProject2` is hidden behind a `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

# The issue

The unit test failed with a `MissingMethodException`

```
[xUnit.net 00:00:00.38]     TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [FAIL]
  Failed TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [2 ms]
  Error Message:
   System.MissingMethodException : Method not found: 'Void ClassLibrary2.Class2.Class2Test1()'.
  Stack Trace:
     at ClassLibrary1.Class1.Class1Test1()
   at TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1() in C:\Users\rex\source\netstandard-bug-repro\TestProject1\UnitTest1.cs:line 12
```

# Expected result

The compiler should have resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.0)*` 

# Actual result

The compiler resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.1)*` 

Which causes the exception because the offending method, `ClassProject2Test1`, was hidden by the `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1" (#1787)

Issues.Title: Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions
Issues.Body:
### Problem
There is a security vulnerability with the version of System.Text.RegularExpressions that is used by dotnet standard. The vulnerable version of System.Text.RegularExpressions is 4.3.0. Please see links below for the vulnerability documentation or discussion:

https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2019-0820
https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/111
https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2019-0820
https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-DOTNET-SYSTEMTEXTREGULAREXPRESSIONS-174708
https://www.whitesourcesoftware.com/vulnerability-database/CVE-2019-0820

The dotnet commit that fixed the vulnerability is https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/commit/19d4b1163d8a03dd90ff5fd1785eea6305112545

### Issue:
We use whitesource and it has caught this issue with high severity. We don't consume System.Text.RegularExpressions directly but packages that use this. Therefore as a transitive dependency due to NetStandard library, which is being used by several other dotnet packages like Castle Windsor, MassTransit etc., Once an update is available the others could followup and update.

### Code:

[The latest version 2.0.3 of Net standard ](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) still seem to be using System.Text.RegularExpressions version 4.3.0 as per https://github.com/dotnet/standard/blob/master/src/apicompat/netstandard/netstandard.depproj

### Fix
Please update[ library](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) targeting .netStandard 1.6 to update System.Text.RegularExpression package to latest secured version 4.3.1 to fix the security issue or kindly suggest alternatives.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions" (#1786)

Issues.Title: linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem
Issues.Body:
Hello,

I am currently using .NET core 2.2.x and EF Core. 2.2.6. I have a function that returns a List<Animal> from the database with no issue. It returns 11 results. However, when I try to use `.Where(p => p.DeletedAt.GetValueOrDefault(DateTime.Now) => DateTime.Now).ToList()`, it still should return 11 results, however it returns 0. I also eliminated the possibility that there is something wrong with my where clause (logic) because it works perfectly on 4.6.1 EF Core 2.2.6. Furthermore, I confirmed that it is only where I am comparing a nullable type using that function and I am guessing that I missed a thread someone opened on this issue. I am aware .NET core 2.2 is not LTS. I also thought this goes here because it's not AFAIK, an EF core issue but rather an Ienumerable/Linq issue.

Update: As it turns out your notion of `DateTime.Now` getting evaluated twice is true. To rectify that, I will now be using `DateTime.Now.Date`. This is odd because this exact code works on 4.6.1. You're probably right. SMH. Thank you @GrabYourPitchforks! You may now close.

> sn.exe -v Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll

Microsoft (R) .NET Framework Strong Name Utility Version 4.0.30319.0
Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. All rights reserved.

Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll is a delay-signed or test-signed assembly

Additional information:

- The assembly versions `161.46041.41` and `161.46367.54` ended up in the same result
- This issue looks very similar to [this](https://www.damirscorner.com/blog/posts/20140502-StrongNameValidationFailedSecurityException.html)
- @markingmyname / @olprod: The root package, which is required for [Server Management Objects (SMOs)](https://docs.microsoft.com/sql/relational-databases/server-management-objects-smo/overview-smo?view=sql-server-ver15), is:

Issues.Title: System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings slow
Issues.Body:
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity2.visualstudio.com/t/SystemDrawingPrintingPrinterSettings-/890524)._ --- Hello I'm debugging a problem with the printer settings. Some calls are significant slower if the default printer is a network printer, even if I explicit set a local printer name. After studying referencesource I think I found the culprit. I call: var printerSettings = new System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings(); printerSettings.PrinterName = "LOCALPRINTER"; // the next call is slow if the OS default printer is a network printer var res = printerSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PrinterResolution Internally FastDeviceCapabilities is called. FastDeviceCapabilities calls GetOutputPort. But GetOutput port return the port of the default printer and not the port of the given printer! In addition, DeviceCapabilities is then called with a wrong combination of printer name and port, don't know if this could lead to additional problems. Resolution: GetOutputPort should return the port of the given printer and not accessing the default printer at all. Best Regards, Raphael --- ### Original Comments #### Raphael Affolter on 1/20/2020, 04:03 AM:

I forgot to mention: .Net Framework 4.6.1

Because we print a lot, we really suffer from this performance penalty.

Raphael

Issues.Title: Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF
Issues.Body:
I'm working on converting a large WPF solution's projects to SDK style and ran into some issues.

The solution is large with multiple projects(old style) all targeting .net452 and some nugets(some made by me) installed, targeting both .net452 and .netstandard2.1 This all seems to work fine, somehow the nuget manages to install the correct version targeting .net452.

I have decided to slowly convert the projects inside the solution to SDK style targeting .net452 and .netstandard2.1 just like the nugets.

This is where the problem starts, one project was converted so far that is referenced by multiple other projects. Localy everything seems to build and run fine, however when Azure DevOps(VS version 2019) is used to build the solution there are 2 scenarios:

1. The famous error message is shown:

                "Error CS0012: The type 'Object' is defined in an assembly that is not referenced. You must add a reference to assembly 
                 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0"

2. It builds fine but on app launch it crashes with:

                 "Could not load file or assembly 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' 
                 or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified."

I'm suspecting that the problem is related to referencing the SDK project, it looks like that somehow it references the .netstandard2.1 instead of the .net452.

The reason this is my suspicion is that if targetframework is set to only .net452 on the referenced project everything works fine. Google has led me to two possible solutions to tell the project what framework to use from the reference:

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj"
                  AdditionalProperties="TargetFramework=net452">
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
and

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj">
      <SetTargetFramework>TargetFramework=net452</SetTargetFramework>
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <<Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
This doesn't look like it's doing anything and the problem still persists. At the moment I ran out of ideas and I'm here asking for help. Please let me know what I'm doing wrong or what else I can try.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF" (#1776)

As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

Issues.Title: Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths
Issues.Body:
## Customer Impact

A customer reported in dotnet/runtime#71607 that decrypting RSA OAEP with SHA2 and a 3072-bit key on Linux resulted in a OAEP de-padding error, while other platforms were able to perform these operations successfully.

Investigation in to the issue led to uncover that RSA OAEP decryption that uses the managed implementation does not work with non-power-of-two keys because we do not slice a rented buffer accordingly. The current implementation only works because `CryptoPool.Rent` happens to give back power-of-two arrays which are exactly the same size as the key.

The fix is to slice the data to the correct size.

This does not affect dotnet/runtime because the managed implementation of RSA OAEP is no longer used for OpenSSL RSA decryption. This change was introduced in dotnet/runtime#50063.

## Testing

Unit tests were introduced to test RSA OAEP encryption with a 3072-bit RSA key. These tests will be forward-ported to dotnet/runtime.

## Risk

Minimal. The change is localized and understood that a `Slice` was missing.

Issues.Title: Razor component binding can resolve a different type when names collide
Issues.Body:
Razor can bind a component from a referenced assembly, but the generated C# can resolve a different type with the same name in the current project.

For example, a referenced library contains a component:

```csharp
namespace Library;

public class Button : Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.ComponentBase { }
```

The app contains a different, non-component type with the same name:

```csharp
namespace Library;

public class Button { }
```

And an app component imports the library's namespace:

```razor
@using Library

<Button />
```

Razor finds the referenced component and generates:

```csharp
__builder.OpenComponent<global::Library.Button>(0);
```

C# resolves `global::Library.Button` to the app's type, so the generated code fails with `CS0311` because that type isn't a component. There can also be a `CS0436` warning about the conflicting types. `global::` identifies the root namespace, not an assembly.

With the component alias support in [dotnet/roslyn#86372](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/86372), both of these have the same problem:

```razor
@using B = global::Library.Button

<B />
```

```razor
@using UI = global::Library

<UI.Button />
```

For the type alias, C# resolves `B` to the app's class, but Razor matches the library's component by name. The alias target map also compares equal when the alias changes from the library's component to the app's class, so incremental generation may not notice the change.

Razor shouldn't generate a component call that resolves to a different type from the one it bound.

I reproduced the three cases with the current compiler using a matching component descriptor. The ordinary-import path appears to predate the alias PR based on the old source, but I haven't run the example against the old compiler itself.

Issues.Title: Change Signature: keep positional arguments after an in-position named argument
Issues.Body:
Fixes #62824.

The issue shows two problems when removing the `language` parameter of `AbstractBuiltInCodeStyleDiagnosticAnalyzer`'s constructor:

1. In VB, the `[option]:=` argument next to `language:=` was removed too.
2. In C#, at a call like `base(diagnosticId: ..., EnforceOnBuildValues.X, CodeStyleOptions2.Y, language: null!, title: ..., messageFormat: ...)`, the positional arguments after `diagnosticId:` were rewritten as named arguments (`enforceOnBuild:`, `option:`).

The first one no longer reproduces on `main`: it was fixed along with #66547, which covered escaped named arguments like `[new]:=`. I added a test for the exact VB call from the issue so it stays fixed.

This PR fixes the second one.

## Root cause

`PermuteArguments` and `AddNewArgumentsToList` both name every argument that comes after a named one. That was required before C# 7.2 / VB 15.5, but a named argument in its own position can now be followed by positional arguments, and the call in the issue relies on that (`diagnosticId:` is first and in position). So removing an unrelated parameter added names to arguments that didn't need them.

## Fix

In both places, a named argument no longer forces names on the arguments after it when:

- the call already has a positional argument after a named one (so the language version allows it), and
- the named argument is in its own position after the change.

Calls whose named arguments are all trailing keep the old behavior, since they may target a language version without non-trailing named arguments. Arguments that move out of position are still named as before.

## Tests

- C#: `RemoveParameters_NamedArgumentInPositionKeepsOtherArgumentsPositional`, the call from the issue. It fails on `main` (`enforceOnBuild: 0`) and passes with the fix.
- VB: `RemoveParameters_AfterEscapedNamedArgument`, the `[option]:=` call from the issue. It passes on `main` and with the fix.

Local runs:

- `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.EditorFeatures.UnitTests` (net472), tests matching `ChangeSignature`: 419 passed, 0 failed.
- `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.VisualBasic.EditorFeatures.UnitTests` (net472), tests matching `ChangeSignature`: 318 passed, 0 failed.
- `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Features.UnitTests` (net10.0), tests matching `ChangeSignature`, `AddParameter` or `IntroduceParameter`: 187 passed, 0 failed.
- `dotnet format whitespace --verify-no-changes` passes on the changed files.

Issues.Title: Memory-safety V2 crashes the compiler on a nullable generic override return type
Issues.Body:
**Version Used**

- .NET SDK 11.0.100: C# compiler `5.12.0-1.26529.118` (`297acf930fb0f5c07fd4e51d78e521b4ad2e5d1f`).
- Local Roslyn bootstrap compiler `5.14.0-dev.26560.1`.
- Reproduced on Linux with both compilers.

**Steps to Reproduce**

Add this test to `UnsafeEvolutionTests` in `src/Compilers/CSharp/Test/CSharp15/UnsafeEvolutionTests.cs`:

```csharp
[Theory]
[InlineData(false)]
[InlineData(true)]
public void OverrideWithNullableTypeParameterInGenericReturnType(bool useUpdatedMemorySafetyRules)
{
    var source = """
        #nullable enable
        using System.Threading.Tasks;

        abstract class Base
        {
            public abstract Task<T?> M<T>();
        }

        sealed class Derived : Base
        {
            public override Task<T?> M<T>() where T : default => null!;
        }
        """;

    CreateCompilation(source,
        targetFramework: TargetFramework.NetCoreApp,
        parseOptions: TestOptions.RegularPreview,
        options: TestOptions.UnsafeReleaseDll.WithUpdatedMemorySafetyRules(useUpdatedMemorySafetyRules))
        .VerifyEmitDiagnostics();
}
```

The source also reproduces the crash when compiled directly with `/langversion:preview /unsafe+ /memorysafetyrulesversion:2` using the bootstrap compiler, or `/features:updated-memory-safety-rules` using the compiler shipped in SDK 11.0.100.

**Expected Behavior**

Both theory cases compile successfully.

**Actual Behavior**

The source compiles under memory-safety V1, but compilation under V2 crashes with a `NullReferenceException`. Direct command-line compilation under V2 aborts the compiler process with exit code 134, rather than producing a diagnostic.

An abbreviated stack from the bootstrap compiler:

```text
System.NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object.
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Symbols.TypeWithAnnotations.IsVoidType()
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Symbols.MemberSignatureComparer.HaveSameReturnTypes(...)
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Symbols.MemberSignatureComparer.Equals(...)
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Symbols.OverriddenOrHiddenMembersHelpers.FindOverriddenOrHiddenMembersInType(...)
   ...
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Symbols.OverriddenMethodTypeParameterMap.GetOverriddenMethod(...)
   ...
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Symbols.TypeWithAnnotations.LazyNullableTypeParameter.GetResolvedType()
   ...
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Binder.ReportDiagnosticsIfUnsafeMemberAccess[T](...)
   ...
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Symbols.SourceOrdinaryMethodSymbol.MakeParametersAndBindReturnType(...)
```

Issues.Title: IDE0059: don't report writes read after a recursive local function call returns
Issues.Body:
Fixes #58407.

IDE0059 reports the last `i += 1` here as unnecessary, but removing it changes the result:

```cs
int i = 0;
int Recurse()
{
    if (i > 10) return i;
    i += 1;
    var a = Recurse();
    i += 1;
    var b = Recurse();
    i += 1; // IDE0059
    return a + b;
}
return Recurse();
```

## Root cause

`SymbolUsageAnalysis` analyzes a local function invocation by walking the function's flow graph. To stop at a recursive invocation, it resets the state at the call site, which marks every write that reaches the call as read. That covers writes made *before* a recursive call, but not writes made after the last one: those reach the end of the function, flow back into the recursive call site in the caller's frame, and are read by the code after the call (`i += 1` after `var a = Recurse()` above). Nothing marked them as read.

## Fix

- `LambdaOrLocalFunctionsBeingAnalyzed` becomes a dictionary that also records whether a recursive invocation of the function was found during its analysis.
- After analyzing an invocation that turned out to be recursive, the writes that reach the end of the function are marked as read, if they are made inside the function's body to variables declared outside of it. Variables declared inside the function, including its parameters, are separate in each invocation, so their writes can't flow back to a caller and are still reported.
- The same applies to lambdas invoked recursively through a delegate.

## Tests

New tests in `RemoveUnusedValueAssignmentTests`:

- `WriteAfterLastRecursiveInvocation_ReadByRecursiveCaller`: the case from the issue.
- `WriteAfterLastRecursiveInvocation_ReadByRecursiveCaller_Lambda`: the same with a recursive lambda.
- `WriteAfterLastRecursiveInvocation_LocalDeclaredInsideFunction`: a dead write to a local declared inside the recursive function is still reported and fixed.

The first two (4 test cases) fail on `main` and pass with the fix. The third passes on both.

Local runs (net10.0 / net10.0-windows):

- `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Features.UnitTests`, tests matching `RemoveUnused`: 1060 passed, 0 failed.
- `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.VisualBasic.Features.UnitTests`, tests matching `RemoveUnused`: 12 passed, 0 failed.
- `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Workspaces.UnitTests`: 1230 passed, 0 failed.
- `dotnet format whitespace --verify-no-changes` passes on the changed files.

`SymbolUsageAnalysis` is only used by the IDE0059/IDE0060 analyzer, which is why the runs above focus on its tests.

Issues.Title: Reindent lambda and anonymous method bodies moved to a new line by formatting
Issues.Body:
Fixes #71637.

"Use block body for property" on

```cs
Action A => delegate
{
};
```

produces a `return delegate` whose braces stay at the property's indentation instead of following the `return`. Same for `() => { }`.

## Root cause

Lambda and anonymous method bodies are anchored: the formatter keeps them at the same offset from the first token of the line their anchor token starts on. That first token is recorded before any formatting is applied. Here it is `Action`, because the unformatted tree has `Action A{get{return delegate` on one line. Formatting then breaks the line so `return delegate` starts a new line at column 12, but the delta is still measured from `Action`, which didn't move, so the body isn't moved either.

## Fix

`FormattingContext.GetAnchorDeltaFromOriginalColumn` now measures from the first token of the line the anchor token is on *after* the earlier formatting operations, when that is a different token from both the recorded one and the anchor token itself. In this case it is `return`, so the body moves by the same amount as the line it now belongs to.

When the anchor token itself starts its line, the old behavior is kept. A first version applied the new measurement in that case too, and changed the output of three VB `ReplacePropertyWithMethods` tests and one C# `ReplaceMethodWithProperty` test. In those, the generated code puts the anchor statement after a newly generated header in the unformatted tree, so neither the old nor the new measurement is meaningful there, and changing them is out of scope for this issue.

## Tests

Three new tests in `UseExpressionBodyForPropertiesRefactoringTests`: an anonymous method body, a lambda body, and an empty lambda body. All three fail on `main` with the body left at column 4, and pass with the fix.

Local runs (net10.0 / net10.0-windows):

- `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Workspaces.UnitTests`: 1230 passed, 0 failed.
- `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.VisualBasic.Workspaces.UnitTests`: 486 passed, 0 failed.
- `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.VisualBasic.Features.UnitTests`: 4059 passed, 0 failed.
- `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Features.UnitTests`, tests matching `UseExpressionBody`, `ReplaceMethodWithProperty`, `ConvertAnonymousFunction` or `Lambda`: 1243 passed, 0 failed. The full suite was run on the first, broader version of the fix (20908 passed, 0 failed, with that version's updated `ReplaceMethodWithProperty` expectation). The final version only restores the previous behavior in more cases, and that expectation is back to its original value.
- `dotnet format whitespace --verify-no-changes` passes on the changed files.

Issues.Title: ObjectFormatter: skip properties of ref struct types instead of throwing
Issues.Body:
Fixes #51548.

`CSharpObjectFormatter.FormatObject` throws `NotSupportedException` when the object has a property whose type is a ref struct:

```cs
ref struct X {}
class Y { public X x => default; }
CSharpObjectFormatter.Instance.FormatObject(new Y()); // throws
```

The formatter reads each property with `PropertyInfo.GetValue`, which can't box a ref struct and throws `NotSupportedException`. `GetMemberValue` only catches `TargetInvocationException`, so the exception escapes `FormatObject`.

## Changes

- `CommonObjectFormatter.Visitor.FormatObjectMembers` skips properties whose type is a ref struct (or a by-ref to one), the same way it already skips indexers. There is no value it could show for them.
- New `ObjectFormatterHelpers.IsByRefLikeType`. `Type.IsByRefLike` isn't available on netstandard2.0, so it looks for the `IsByRefLikeAttribute` the compiler puts on ref structs.

The fix is in the shared visitor, so the VB formatter gets it too.

## Tests

`ObjectFormatterTests.RefStructPropertiesAreSkipped` formats an object with an `int` property and a ref struct property, and expects only the `int` property in the output. It fails on `main` with the `NotSupportedException` from the issue and passes with the fix.

Local runs:

- `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Scripting.UnitTests`: 269 passed (net10.0) and 280 passed (net472), 0 failed.
- `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Scripting.UnitTests`: 45 passed on net10.0 and net472.
- `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.VisualBasic.Scripting.UnitTests` (net472): 33 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `TestDisplayResultsWithCurrentUICulture1`, which fails the same way on `main` on this machine (non-English Windows culture), so it isn't related to this change.
- `dotnet format whitespace --verify-no-changes` passes on the changed files.

Issues.Title: Fix stale source generator diagnostics in Hot Reload
Issues.Body:

Report only diagnostics from the new snapshot while retaining old diagnostics in the trace log. Add regression coverage for clean/error transitions and verify that reported diagnostics belong to the current snapshot.

Fixes #86336.

Issues.Title: Use a GitHub App token for the Roslyn PR tagger
Issues.Body:
## Summary
- Replace the PR tagger PAT input with a short-lived installation token for `dotnet Roslyn Issue Tagger` (App ID 5701303).
- Check out the repository for the shared Arcade script, and use `@self` so the token template resolves correctly beneath the external 1ES extends template.
- Keep the existing PAT mapping unchanged until the actual tagger succeeds with the App token.

## Provisioning verified
- Secret Manager manifest merged: https://github.com/dotnet/arcade/pull/17783.
- Initialized App credential projections in EngKeyVault through Secret Manager, including rotation metadata.
- Existing `Roslyn PRTagger: DevDiv` WIF principal has Secrets User only on the two exact App credential secret scopes; no vault-wide grant.
- Stored credentials authenticate as the expected App, with Issues write and Metadata read.
- Installation 180677353 contains exactly `dotnet/roslyn` and `dotnet/fsharp`; installation-token issue searches passed on both. Temporary token revoked; local key copy removed.
- Ownership transfer to `dotnet` is requested but still pending acceptance; current owner remains `dotnet-bot`.

## Validation
- YAML parsing, required-template-parameter/path assertions, checkout/token-binding checks and `git diff --check` pass.
- Actual consumer pipeline 1333 dry-run compilation with this PR YAML succeeds and includes token minting and tagger tasks. The dry run does not execute the tagger.
- Isolated WIF canary [3132307](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_build/results?buildId=3132307) **succeeded**: actual tagger WIF identity -> both exact Key Vault secret scopes -> shared Arcade helper -> installation token -> exact repository scope and successful issue searches on both repositories. Token revoked afterward. No issues created or changed.
- Canary compilation caught the missing `@self` qualifier; corrected in e8276021136.

## Remaining gates
Keep this PR draft pending human review and explicit production rollout authorization. Full tagger execution/issue creation is not yet validated. No production pipeline run or merge was performed. After an explicitly authorized rollout, verify the actual consumer succeeds before removing the PAT mapping or revoking the PAT; first confirm no remaining consumers.

Related: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_workitems/edit/12159.

Canary cleanup verified: scratch repository deleted, pipeline 1722 disabled, and scratch endpoint/agent-queue authorizations revoked. Successful run retained as evidence.

Issues.Title: [Razor] Generic component inheritance causes duplicate parameter diagnostics (RZ10009)
Issues.Body:
## Problem
Razor reports RZ10009 (Duplicate component parameter) when using a generic component through a C# shorthand class that inherits from another generic component with mapped type parameters

## Reproduction

### Foo.razor
```cs
@typeparam T1
@typeparam T2

@code {
 [Parameter]
 public T1 First {get; set;}

 [Parameter]
 public T2 Second {get; set;}
}
```

### SimpleFoo.cs
```cs
public class Foo<T> : Foo<T, T>;
```

### Home.razor
```cs
 <!-- RZ10009 at "First" and "Second"-->
<Foo T="int" First="42" Second="600">
```



### Expected behavior
The component should compile successfully against the single generic type

## Additional observations
* Deleting `bin` and `obj` and rebuilding does not resolve the issue
* Renaming the shorthand class to something else, eg `SimpleFoo<T>` solves the issue
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "[Razor] Generic component inheritance causes duplicate parameter diagnostics (RZ10009)" (#86373)

Issues.Title: Support aliases in Razor `@using` directives
Issues.Body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/85411

This is obviously a big one, I'm hoping commit-at-a-time makes it somewhat easier, but who knows. Expecting there will be a bunch of comments, both from humans and copilot, as I am most definitely not a compiler engineer, so if there are better approaches to things, or things should happen at different layers etc. I'm all ears.

Earlier attempts did do more at different phases, but in the end keeping it all in the binding phase seemed to me to be the most logical and readable. There is plenty of perf improvements to be had my using multiple CWTs and caching things across phases etc., and a lot of that code was written, but I'd prefer to prove the feature first.

Issues.Title: [Security] Create dotnet-watch solution files privately
Issues.Body:
## Summary
- create generated dotnet-watch solution files atomically under a unique private temporary directory
- keep the generated solution open with read-only sharing while child build processes consume it
- clean up individual files and the private directory through the watch context lifetime

This is a forward port for the publicly disclosed [CVE-2026-114155](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-114155).

## Validation
- `dotnet build test/dotnet-watch.Tests/dotnet-watch.Tests.csproj -c Debug -f net12.0 --no-restore`: passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors
- focused runtime check verified create-new behavior, child-process read sharing, denied write sharing, and cleanup
- the repository test executable could not enter test discovery because its module initializer requires the full SDK redist layout; normal CI is required to run `TemporaryFileManagerTests`

Issues.Title: Reduce CA1851 and shared dataflow analysis overhead
Issues.Body:
> [!NOTE]
> Drafted with AI assistance.

## Summary

Reduce CA1851 and shared dataflow-analysis overhead by avoiding unnecessary analysis and repeated tracking, lookup, and reporting work.

- Add conservative CA1851 source pre-analysis, bound repeated deferred-path expansion, and share enumeration-reporting state.
- Index operation and child-entity lookups, group argument postprocessing by parent, reuse unchanged abstract values, and remove redundant taint discovery and formatting.
- Make CFG/result caches compilation-owned, preserve canonical live CFG identity, and include supported-type and mapping policies in cache keys without retaining pooled callback state.
- Correct entity/location/index equality and normalize named-indexer keys by bound parameter order while preserving argument evaluation order.

Rule IDs, defaults, and severities are unchanged.

## Performance

Focused synthetic workloads, comparing preserved pre-optimization component baselines with the final Release implementation; compiler binding is excluded. The CA1851 baseline already includes the original narrow one-direct-input shortcut.

| Workload | Elapsed time, before -> after | Managed allocation, before -> after |
|---|---|---|
| 256 once-used enumerable aliases | 55-56 -> 7.6 ms (**86% less**) | 7.43 -> 2.85 MB (**62% less**) |
| 256 once-used LINQ pipelines | 146-151 -> 46-48 ms (**69% less**) | 32.86 -> 16.12 MB (**51% less**) |
| 256 inputs, eight enumerations each: 2,048 sites | 1.50-1.58 s -> 85-89 ms (**94% less**) | 43.48 -> 26.84 MB (**38% less**) |
| Shared flow: 1,024 locals, 256 uncertain-index writes | 61-65 -> 36 ms (**42% less**) | 14.64 -> 5.29 MB (**64% less**) |

Times are ranges of run medians from baseline/final ABBA comparisons, with three warmups and seven CA1851 or twelve shared-flow measured samples per run. Allocation figures are rounded means of the two per-run medians; MB denotes decimal megabytes.

These are component-level results, **not end-to-end project-build or peak-memory savings**. Smaller and mixed-analyzer workloads were not uniformly faster.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Reduce CA1851 and shared dataflow analysis overhead" (#57054)

Issues.Title: Allow extending metadata preserved by GetCopyToPublishDirectoryItems
Issues.Body:
`GetCopyToPublishDirectoryItems` drops metadata outside a fixed allowlist, preventing downstream SDKs from consuming custom metadata from local or referenced-project items.

- **Extensibility**
  - Adds `MSBuildGetCopyToPublishDirectoryAdditionalItemMetadataToCopy`.
  - Appends its semicolon-separated values to the optimized metadata allowlist.

- **Behavior**
  - Preserves requested metadata for current and referenced projects.
  - Retains existing filtering when the property is unset.

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <MSBuildGetCopyToPublishDirectoryAdditionalItemMetadataToCopy>
    $(MSBuildGetCopyToPublishDirectoryAdditionalItemMetadataToCopy);PublishFolderType
  </MSBuildGetCopyToPublishDirectoryAdditionalItemMetadataToCopy>
</PropertyGroup>
```

The property must be configured in every project where publish-item filtering occurs.

- Fixes #57024

Issues.Title: dotnetup: Reconsider support for stable-branded preview builds
Issues.Body:
#56913 added support for installing stable-branded non-final builds.  We may want to reconsider how we support this.

## Stable Branding

Preview and Release Candidate builds of .NET use `-preview.x` or `-rc.x` semantic versions, and the full semantic version is reflected in the build's branding and in the SDK folder on disk.

However, after RC2 (and for our servicing builds), we produce builds using stable branding.  So the build number may be something like `11.0.100-rtm.26552.115`, but when it installs on disk it is branded as `11.0.100`.

The stable branded builds also depend on packages (such as targeting packs, runtime packs, Analyzers, AOT tooling, etc) with stable branding.  Because the versions of these packages don't change, and because a given package version on a feed is immutable, these packages are not published to the standard dotnet package feed, rather there is a separate feed with the packages for each build.  So to use the build you need to set up a special NuGet feed.  You also may need to take care to clear all of the local NuGet caches when installing a newer build with the same version number.

## Dotnetup support

We had to add a lot of complexity in #56913 to handle stable branded versions.  There is still further behavior to consider to support updating from one stable branded build to another one: https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56921

However, even if dotnetup supports installing stable-branded builds, they will still not be very usable, with the feed configuration and build identity issues.  I think that it is better to consider usage of stable-branded builds a scenario that is mostly internal to Microsoft for testing the builds before they are released, rather than something that most developers (even the "power users") would use.

I suggest the following:

### Don't include stable branded builds in channels such as `11.0-daily`

The reason we added the support in the first place was because the RTM stable-branded builds started showing up in the daily channels, and installation would fail.  We should exclude stable-branded but non-final builds from all of the current channels we have (daily, preview, etc).

This would mean that to install one of these builds you would have to specify the explicit full build number.

### Require `--untracked` to install stable-branded non-final builds

Most of the complexity in #56913 had to do with keeping track of the difference between the branded version of the build and the full build version.  We can probably avoid most of that complexity by only supporting installing these builds in `--untracked` mode, where we don't have to keep track of that information.

This is probably reasonable to do because the feed setup and package caching issues mean that these builds will generally be used in testing environments, not in long-lived dotnet roots where dotnetup would need to track versions over time and keep them up-to-date.

## Feedback and future

Making these changes wouldn't prevent us from adding more support in the future, but would help make sure that the support would be driven by feedback and usage scenarios.

We are interested in feedback in how people would like to use `-rtm` and `-servicing` builds, and how this proposal would affect this usage.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "dotnetup: Reconsider support for stable-branded preview builds" (#57052)

Issues.Title: Use proper Registry Lookup for 64 Bit Machines in `dotnetup`
Issues.Body:
`sharedhost` is not in the 32-bit view on 64-bit machines, which means we don't follow the proper path precedence search. The legacy logic _was_ and _is_ correct for `installedhost` because "win64=no" in `host.wxs` as referenced in the source code comment.

The end result is that we may not properly resolve the system path on 64-bit machines.

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-114155 - .NET Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in the .NET SDK's dotnet-watch component. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected SDK installations. A local attacker who can replace or modify a temporary solution file used by dotnet-watch can alter a subsequent build. The fix stores generated solution files in a private temporary directory and keeps each file open with read-only sharing while the build uses it. ## Announcement Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/502 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-367 - **MSRC severity:** Important - **Impact:** Elevation of Privilege ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux, macOS. - **Architectures:** Linux: Arm, Arm64, x64; macOS: Arm64, x64 Windows is outside this advisory's affected scope when its temporary directory is private to the current user, as assumed by the implementation. Shared or insecurely configured Windows temporary directories are not covered by that assumption. ## Affected Packages The .NET SDK includes dotnet-watch and the Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch assembly. Each SDK feature band is a separate servicing line. Update an affected 10.0.3xx installation to the fixed 10.0.4xx SDK listed below. ### .NET SDK 10.0.3xx Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [.NET SDK (dotnet-watch) 10.0.3xx](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/10.0) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.303 | 10.0.404 ### .NET SDK 10.0.4xx Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [.NET SDK (dotnet-watch) 10.0.4xx](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/10.0) | >= 10.0.400, <= 10.0.403 | 10.0.404 ### .NET SDK 11.0.1xx Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [.NET SDK (dotnet-watch) 11.0.1xx](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0) | >= 11.0.100-preview.3.26207.106, <= 11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148 | 11.0.100 ### Separately restored Aspire watch tool Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.303 | 10.0.404 [Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire) | >= 10.0.400, <= 10.0.403 | 10.0.404 [Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire) | >= 11.0.100-preview.3.26207.106, <= 11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148 | 11.0.100 This tool has its own copy of the watch implementation. Updating the SDK does not necessarily replace a separately restored tool. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Run `dotnet --version` from the directory where you run dotnet-watch to identify the selected SDK. Use `dotnet --info` and `dotnet --list-sdks` to check its installation path, OS, architecture, and other installed SDKs. Check the nearest applicable `global.json`, including its `version` and `rollForward` settings: installing a newer SDK does not necessarily change the SDK selected for a pinned project. See [.NET SDK selection](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/versions/selection). Review use of dotnet-watch against the affected intervals above. Membership in a listed feature band alone does not establish that a specific SDK version is vulnerable. For Aspire or other tooling that separately restores Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire, check the actual restored package version separately from the selected SDK. ### How do I fix the issue? The fixed SDK versions are 10.0.404 and 11.0.100, as applicable. Update each affected SDK installation and restart dotnet-watch. For SDKs installed through Visual Studio, update Visual Studio to a release that includes a fixed SDK. Updating only an application runtime does not replace SDK-bundled tools. Ensure that `global.json` and its SDK roll-forward policy select a fixed SDK, then rerun `dotnet --version` in the working directory to verify the selection. The SDK-bundled watch tool is installed beneath that selected SDK's `DotnetTools/dotnet-watch` directory.
