Issues.Title: dotnetup garbage collection deletes workload sets, manifests and packs installed by `dotnet workload`
Issues.Body:
## Summary

dotnetup's garbage collector deletes content installed by `dotnet workload`, because that content is not recorded in `dotnetup_manifest.json`. Workload install state lives under `metadata`, which GC skips, so it survives and keeps pointing at the deleted workload set. After that, `dotnet workload repair` fails because the workload version recorded in `InstallState/default.json` cannot be found.

Seen repeatedly on one install. Environment: macOS arm64, dotnetup `0.3.0-preview.1.26554.3+a98e2d0757a95d8e147c63e71bf5f2c9f2633a26`.

## Cause

[`GarbageCollector.FindOrphanedSubcomponents`](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/a98e2d0757a95d8e147c63e71bf5f2c9f2633a26/src/Installer/dotnetup.Library/GarbageCollector.cs#L167-L200) walks the dotnet root at the depths defined in `SubcomponentResolver` and treats every folder that no remaining installation references as an orphan.

`Installation.Subcomponents` is built from the SDK archive contents, so anything `dotnet workload` added is never referenced:

- `sdk-manifests/10.0.400/workloadsets/10.0.403` matches `sdk-manifests` depth 4 and is deleted.
- Workload manifest versions at `sdk-manifests/<band>/<manifest id>/<version>` that did not come from the archive are deleted.
- Workload packs at `packs/<pack id>/<version>` are deleted.

`metadata` is an ignored folder, so `metadata/workloads/<arch>/<band>/InstallState/default.json` and `InstalledWorkloads` are left behind, describing content that no longer exists.

The logic is unchanged on `release/dnup` as of 47d2c9d.

## Evidence from the affected install

- `InstallState/default.json` for band 10.0.400 contains `"workloadVersion": "10.0.403"`, and `sdk-manifests/10.0.400/workloadsets` is empty.
- `dotnet-sdk-10.0.403-osx-arm64.tar.gz` and the 10.0.404 tarball contain no `workloadsets` folder, so the set came from `dotnet workload`.
- `sdk-manifests/10.0.400/workloadsets` and `sdk-manifests/11.0.100-rc.3/workloadsets` were both modified at the same second, in the same minute dotnetup installed new SDKs. There was no `dotnet workload` history entry for that band at that time.
- 88 `packs/<pack id>` folders were left empty in that same minute, with similar batches of empty folders at earlier times that SDK tarballs were downloaded.

I do not have a log showing which dotnetup command ran. In the source, GC is reached from the update and uninstall workflows.

## Expected repro

These steps are derived from the code and the state above. I have not run them on a clean install.

1. `dotnetup sdk install lts`
2. `dotnet workload install maui`, or another workload, using workload-set mode
3. Run `dotnetup update` when a newer SDK is available, or run a `dotnetup` uninstall
4. `dotnet workload repair`

Expected: workloads remain usable, or dotnetup clearly reports that it removed them.

Actual: the workload set and packs are removed, and `dotnet workload repair` fails with the workload version not found.

## Possible fix

Limit deletion to subcomponents listed on the installations being removed, minus those still referenced, rather than scanning the disk for everything unreferenced. The trade-off is that the disk scan also cleans up folders left behind when a run crashes after persisting the manifest, so that case would need separate handling.

Separately, workload content that belongs to an SDK band being removed may need deliberate handling so `metadata/workloads` does not go stale.

## Workaround

After each dotnetup update or uninstall, run `dotnet workload update` and `dotnet workload repair`. If update hits the same missing-set error, rename the stale `InstallState/default.json` first.

Issues.Body:

Issues.Title: dotnet <command> --help shows "app" instead of "dotnet" in the Usage line on macOS/Linux (.NET 11 RTM)
Issues.Body:
### Description

In .NET 11 RTM, help output on non-Windows platforms uses `app` as the root command name instead of `dotnet`. In RC3 it correctly showed `dotnet`. Windows is not affected.

### Repro

On macOS or Linux with SDK 11.0.100:

```
dotnet tool list --help
```

or in a container:

```
docker run --rm -it mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:11.0.100-resolute-aot dotnet tool list --help
```

### Actual (11.0.100 RTM, macOS/Linux)

```
Description:
  List tools installed globally or locally.

Usage:
  app tool list [<packageId>] [options]

Arguments:
  <PACKAGE_ID>  The NuGet Package Id of the tool to list

Options:
  -g, --global           List tools installed for the current user. [default: False]
  --local                List the tools installed in the local tool manifest. [default: False]
  --tool-path <PATH>     The directory containing the tools to list.
  --format <json|table>  The output format for the list of tools. [default: table]
  -?, -h, --help         Show command line help.
```

### Expected (as in RC3, and as on Windows in RTM)

```
Usage:
  dotnet tool [command] [options]
```

For reference, RC3 output for `dotnet tool list -h`:

```
Description:
  List tools installed globally or locally.

Usage:
  dotnet tool list [<packageId>] [options]

Arguments:
  <PACKAGE_ID>  The NuGet Package Id of the tool to list

Options:
  -g, --global           List tools installed for the current user. [default: False]
  --local                List the tools installed in the local tool manifest. [default: False]
  --tool-path <PATH>     The directory containing the tools to list.
  --format <json|table>  The output format for the list of tools. [default: table]
  -?, -h, --help         Show command line help.
```

### Environment

- SDK: 11.0.100 (RTM)
- Last known good: 11.0.100-rc.3
- Reproduced on: macOS, Ubuntu (native install), Ubuntu container (`sdk:11.0.100-resolute-aot`)
- Not reproduced on: Windows (Usage line correctly shows `dotnet`)

### Notes

- This only happens on non-Windows platforms. On Windows the root command name is correctly `dotnet`, but on macOS and Linux it comes out as `app`. System.CommandLine derives that name from the executable or entry-assembly name, so the way the name is resolved probably differs between the Windows and Unix hosts.

Issues.Title: SDK 11.0.100 GA: `dotnet --version` waits 4.5 s and `dotnet build` 9 s at exit on a Linux machine where 169.254.169.254 does not answer
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

On a Linux machine that is not an Azure VM, every `dotnet` command under SDK 11.0.100 (GA) waits several seconds before exiting: `dotnet --version` takes 4.5 s and a no-op `dotnet build` takes 9.3 s. SDK 10.0.404 on the same machine takes 0.06 s and 0.7 s. The time is spent waiting on connections to the Azure VM metadata address `169.254.169.254:80`, which never complete there.

This is the behaviour reported in #56928 and #56815, which were closed as fixed for 11.0.0 by #56863. It still happens on the GA SDK, and the wait is longer than in those reports.

### Steps to reproduce

On a Linux machine where connections to `169.254.169.254` are silently dropped (`curl -m 12 http://169.254.169.254/` times out), with telemetry at its default:

```sh
mkdir repro && cd repro
echo '{"sdk":{"version":"11.0.100","rollForward":"disable"}}' > global.json
dotnet new console -o app && cd app
dotnet build

time dotnet --version
time dotnet build
time dotnet msbuild -version
```

### Expected behavior

The commands exit as soon as their work is done, as they do with SDK 10.0.404 or with `DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1`.

### Actual behavior

Wall time, three runs each, all within 0.2 s of the figure shown:

| Configuration | `dotnet --version` | `dotnet build` (no-op) | `dotnet msbuild -version` |
|---|---|---|---|
| SDK 10.0.404, default | 0.06 s | 0.7 s | 0.09 s |
| SDK 11.0.100, default | 4.55 s | 9.28 s | 9.2 s |
| SDK 11.0.100, `DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1` | 0.01 s | 0.15 s | 0.08 s |
| SDK 11.0.100, `DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS=0` | 4.54 s | 9.28 s | not measured |
| SDK 11.0.100, default, connections to `169.254.169.254` rejected with a TCP reset (`iptables ... -j REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset`) | 0.55 s | 1.27 s | 1.2 s |

The time is spent waiting, not computing: `dotnet --version` is `real 4.559 user 0.051 sys 0.010`, and MSBuild reports `Time Elapsed 00:00:00.14` for the 9.28 s build.

`strace -f -tt -e trace=connect,exit_group dotnet --version`, times relative to the first connection:

- +0.00 s: `connect` to the telemetry ingestion endpoint on port 443.
- +0.55 s: `connect` to `::ffff:169.254.169.254` port 80 returns `EINPROGRESS` and never completes.
- +2.56 s: a second `connect` to `::ffff:169.254.169.254` port 80.
- +4.56 s: `exit_group(0)`.

So the process makes two metadata attempts and waits 2 s on each. The same trace of `dotnet build` shows that sequence twice in a row (attempts at +0.6 s, +2.6 s, +5.2 s and +7.2 s, exit at +9.2 s), which accounts for the 9 s.

On an Azure-hosted machine (GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` runner), where the metadata address answers in 7 ms, the same SDK takes 0.15 s for `dotnet --version` and 0.57 s for the no-op build.

### Is this a regression?

Yes. SDK 10.0.404 on the same machine is not affected.

### Are there any workarounds?

`DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1` removes the wait.

### dotnet --info output

```
.NET SDK:
 Version:           11.0.100
 Commit:            297acf930f
 Workload version:  11.0.100-manifests.08e30c08
 MSBuild version:   18.12.2-1.26529.118+297acf930

Runtime Environment:
 OS Name:     ubuntu
 OS Version:  24.04
 OS Platform: Linux
 RID:         linux-x64
 Base Path:   /usr/share/dotnet/sdk/11.0.100

Host:
  Version:      11.0.0
  Architecture: x64
  Commit:       297acf930f
```

### Other details

- Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, x64, a hosted CI virtual machine outside Azure. `ip route get 169.254.169.254` resolves through the default gateway; there is no link-local route.
- No `OTEL_*`, `APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_*` or `DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_*` variables set except where the table says so. `DOTNET_NOLOGO=1`, `DOTNET_SKIP_FIRST_TIME_EXPERIENCE=1` and `DOTNET_MULTILEVEL_LOOKUP=0` were set.

Could the metadata request be skipped, or not block process exit, in an 11.0.1xx servicing release?

Found while benchmarking build times for TUnit: https://github.com/thomhurst/TUnit/pull/7707

Issues.Title: Fix native MTP target framework and runtime display
Issues.Body:
Native MTP `dotnet test` currently treats the executing runtime as the test module's target framework. A `net472` application running on .NET Framework 4.8.1 therefore appears as `(net481|x64)`, obscuring which target actually ran.

This change keeps the target TFM and executing process architecture as the primary identity and adds compact runtime information only when it differs:

```text
FrameworkDisplayProbe.exe (net472|x64, runtime: net481)
FrameworkDisplayProbe.exe (net481|x64)
```

- Prefer the evaluated project TFM, then genuine optional `TargetFramework` handshake metadata (field 21). Preserve the existing `Framework` field (2) as runtime information, without a protocol-version bump.
- Keep missing targets unknown: older module-only peers display `(x64, runtime: net481)` instead of inferring a target from the runtime or output directory.
- Apply the same identity across starts, per-test source details, completion, recaps and progress. Ignore modern runtime servicing patches and target platform suffixes only for comparison; preserve full target text and .NET Framework distinctions such as `net48` versus `net481`.
- Reconcile the shared TestFx formatter and contract, retain source-compatible reporter overloads, and reserve primary identity ahead of secondary runtime information in narrow progress frames. Update regression coverage, localized resources and contributor guidance.

### Validation

- 363 focused SDK tests passed through `scripts\RunTests.cs`, including real matching, major-roll-forward and multi-targeted consumers, existing module globbing, and multi-module TRX post-processing.
- All 13 composed-product scenarios passed with the built SDK `12.0.100-dev` and the final source-stamped `Microsoft.Testing.Platform` package `3.0.0-dev.framework7066.final1`: project/module identity, matching runtimes, `net8.0` rolling forward to .NET 12, genuinely absent target attributes, actual x86 execution, deliberate failure (exit 2) and zero results (exit 8). Exact execution counts and independent target/process metadata were checked.
- Unchanged released MSTest 4.5.2 / MTP 2.5.2 repro assertions failed under installed SDK `11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148` and passed under the modified SDK. The reverse older-SDK/new-producer direction also passed. This is historical-SDK red/green, not a clean-base, same-version SDK source A/B.
- Vendoring validation passed (37 entries, 54 sources), committed source blobs and adapted formatter parity were verified, and the linked AOT source closure compiled. NativeAOT linking/execution was unavailable because the VC linker is not installed. Widths 40/80/120 were checked at renderer level, separately from actual 80x24 CLI rendering.

### Coordinated upstream source

The shared source is pinned to TestFx commit `c2b618b17ef3ecbf46054cde3785476673ff9f63`. That coordinated revision is not yet available on upstream `microsoft/testfx`; it must land before this vendoring pin is merged. Project runs remain compatible with older MTP packages, while module-only target metadata requires the additive producer support.

Relates to microsoft/testfx#7066

Issues.Body:
## Build Information

Pull request: #57022
Build: [1673312](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1673312)
Affected job: `Dotnet-Format Integration Tests: aspnetcore`.

The external ASP.NET Core formatter fixture fails during bootstrap/restore:

- [Preparation log](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_apis/build/builds/1673312/logs/132): missing GoogleTest/GoogleMock native sources (`C1083`) and an unresolved `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref` package (`NU1102`).
- [Formatting task log](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_apis/build/builds/1673312/logs/133): the missing GoogleTest/GoogleMock sources recur when the verifier invokes the fixture bootstrap again.

## Failure

The compiler cannot open `gmock-all.cc` and `gtest-all.cc` under `src\submodules\googletest`. The preparation log also reports:

```text
error NU1102: Unable to find package Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref with version ...
```

This issue tracks the fixture's setup failures together; it does not assume that the missing native sources and unresolved reference pack have a single underlying cause.

The [fixture checkout](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/16e3002500949108ae7bce2b12ea35be79c5c7e5/eng/dotnet-format/format-verifier.ps1#L38-L44) fetches/checks out the configured commit but does not initialize submodules. The verifier then [invokes the fixture's build script with `-restore`](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/16e3002500949108ae7bce2b12ea35be79c5c7e5/eng/dotnet-format/format-verifier.ps1#L46-L55). The [pipeline selects the ASP.NET Core fixture](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/16e3002500949108ae7bce2b12ea35be79c5c7e5/eng/dotnet-format/dotnet-format-integration.yml#L39-L45).

Failure to initialize the fixture's submodules is consistent with the missing native files. The logs show that the requested reference pack cannot be resolved from the configured sources, but do not establish whether the correct fix is a fixture update, package preparation, or feed configuration.

These are external-fixture setup failures, separate from the ILCompiler audit failure in #57002 and its downstream missing formatter output. The closed formatter-output issue #56982 explicitly left external-repository setup failures unresolved.

Suggested fix: use a supported, reproducibly restorable fixture; initialize its required submodules and arrange for its required reference pack before workspace formatting. Propagate bootstrap failures rather than continuing to formatting.

## Error Message

The alternatives match either specific ASP.NET Core fixture setup diagnostic. The signature contains no SDK/package version, machine path, or agent identifier. Automatic retries are disabled.

```json

}
```

Issues.Title: dotnet test breaking change: Docker warnings and Nano Server test failures
Issues.Body:
# dotnet test breaking change: Docker warnings and Nano Server test failures

This issue affects .NET 8, 9, 10, and 11. After an SDK update, `dotnet test` using VSTest can show artifacts-directory warnings in containers on all four versions. On Nano Server, test runs on all four versions can also fail to complete when the SDK cannot resolve the user's Local AppData directory.

Set `VSTEST_ARTIFACTS_BASE_DIRECTORY` before running the tests: `/tmp` on Linux, or `C:\Windows\Temp` on Nano Server. This workaround addresses both the warnings and the Nano Server failures on .NET 8, 9, 10, and 11.

## Cause and impact

The changed SDK uses a private directory for test-session files needed for attachment post-processing. Its default base is `/run/user/<uid>` on Linux and Local AppData on Windows. Containers can lack these locations.

On Linux, the SDK does not create that base or automatically use `/tmp`. It continues without providing an artifacts directory to VSTest, which tries the same missing base. On Windows, failure to resolve Local AppData stops the run instead on .NET 8, 9, 10, and 11.

When the fallback directory exists, VSTest can save session files there, but it still warns that it did not receive the SDK's directory. The override restores the intended path shared by the SDK and VSTest.

## Warnings and failures

### Linux containers

If the SDK cannot provide an artifacts directory and no attachments are produced, `dotnet test` prints:

> VSTEST_ARTIFACTS_DIRECTORY environment variable was not found, falling back to a user-private temporary directory. This is most likely caused by an outdated Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk package reference in the test project.

The package advice can be misleading. A missing `/run/user/<uid>` directory can cause this warning even when the SDK and `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk` package are up to date and compatible. Here, `<uid>` is the process's effective user ID; root uses `0`.

If attachments are produced, such as a coverage report from `--collect:"XPlat Code Coverage"`, VSTest tries to save the session files needed to process those attachments after the tests finish. If the fallback directory is missing, it prints this warning instead:

> The test session artifacts were not saved: The user-private temporary directory '/run/user/0' does not exist.

The path uses the current user's ID. Other directory-verification failures use the same `The test session artifacts were not saved: ` prefix followed by the specific reason. This warning replaces the missing-variable warning for that collection step; both are not printed together.

The tests continue, and a passing run can exit with code `0` despite either warning. When the fallback directory is missing, the session files are not saved and the SDK skips attachment post-processing. This does not mean the collector's original output files were deleted.

If attachments are produced and the fallback directory exists, VSTest can save the session files there but still prints the missing-variable warning. Saving those files alone does not ensure the SDK finds them for post-processing. When the SDK successfully provides its private directory, neither warning is expected, and it can find the saved session files.

### Nano Server containers

On .NET 8, 9, 10, and 11, failure to resolve Local AppData stops the run instead of only producing a warning. The SDK prints:

> Could not determine a private base directory for the test run: the current user's local application data folder does not exist or could not be resolved. Set the VSTEST_ARTIFACTS_BASE_DIRECTORY environment variable to the directory the artifacts directory should be created under.

The tests fail to complete. This can happen with or without a collector. The base-directory override below bypasses the Local AppData lookup.

## Fix

Set the variable in the container image or CI step that runs `dotnet test`. Updating the images avoids reverting the change or rebuilding .NET, and keeps the directory protection enabled.

Linux shell:

```bash
export VSTEST_ARTIFACTS_BASE_DIRECTORY=/tmp
dotnet test
```

Nano Server, if PowerShell is available:

```powershell
$env:VSTEST_ARTIFACTS_BASE_DIRECTORY = 'C:\Windows\Temp'
dotnet test
```

Linux Dockerfile:

```dockerfile
ENV VSTEST_ARTIFACTS_BASE_DIRECTORY=/tmp
```

Nano Server Dockerfile, using Docker's default backslash escape syntax:

```dockerfile
ENV VSTEST_ARTIFACTS_BASE_DIRECTORY="C:\\Windows\\Temp"
```

For an existing `docker run` command, add `-e VSTEST_ARTIFACTS_BASE_DIRECTORY=/tmp` on Linux, or `-e "VSTEST_ARTIFACTS_BASE_DIRECTORY=C:\Windows\Temp"` on Windows.

The base must be writable by the test process. An explicitly configured base does not need to exist: the SDK creates missing parent directories when it creates its private folder, provided the test process has permission to create them. Choose another suitably protected, writable base if the suggested location is not accessible.

Set `VSTEST_ARTIFACTS_BASE_DIRECTORY`, not `VSTEST_ARTIFACTS_DIRECTORY`. The SDK passes the latter to VSTest. Changing `TMPDIR` or `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` does not change this Linux default.

## Why a shared temporary base is safe

The SDK creates a new random folder for each invocation, named `<sdk_guid>`. It does not place session files directly in the shared base.

- Linux: the standard `/tmp` has mode `1777`. Its sticky bit prevents other ordinary users from deleting or renaming your entries there. The SDK creates `/tmp/<sdk_guid>` with mode `0700`, allowing only its owner to read, write, and enter it. The permissions apply at creation, not just afterwards.
- Windows: the SDK creates `C:\Windows\Temp\<sdk_guid>` with an owner-only access control list (ACL), which defines who can access the folder. It blocks inherited permissions from the shared base. The owner-only rules also apply to files and folders created inside.

These protections isolate different ordinary users. They do not isolate processes running as the same user, or block root or administrators. Keep the base directory's normal protections; do not disable verification or make the SDK's private folder broadly accessible.

The current build failed the restore/build paths with NU1903. Build 1668485, from an earlier commit of the same pull request, reported the same package and advisory and also failed affected Windows/build paths. The two observations are repeated attempts of one PR, not independent recurrence; no passing preceding build is established in the dossier.

## Error Details

Exact excerpt: src\\Layout\\finalizer\\finalizer.csproj(0,0): error NU1903: Warning As Error: Package Microsoft.DotNet.ILCompiler 10.0.12 has a known high severity vulnerability, [https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p3jp-9v83-76w9](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p3jp-9v83-76w9). Restore then reports Build FAILED and exits with code 1.

## Root Cause Analysis

**Observed:** NuGet restore treats the known high-severity advisory for Microsoft.DotNet.ILCompiler 10.0.12 as an error while restoring src\\Layout\\finalizer\\finalizer.csproj; this blocks the affected build and formatting tasks.

**Assessment:** The proximate cause is the package-policy audit finding combined with warning-as-error handling. The dossier supports that this is an SDK CI build break, but does not establish whether the dependency pin, advisory applicability, or branch contents is the intended remediation point.

**Confidence:** High for the observed restore failure and its immediate cause; Medium for SDK ownership/remediation because landed-tree equivalence and dependency history were not verified.

**Alternatives / Unknowns:** The collector did not compare the tested PR merge tree with the landed commit tree. It also does not establish whether a coordinated runtime/ILCompiler update is already present or whether the advisory can be resolved by another dependency change.

## Suggested Investigation

1. Compare the tested merge tree with PR #56977's landed commit and verify the current Microsoft.DotNet.ILCompiler pin in the dependency files.
2. Inspect the restore binlog/project assets and advisory metadata to confirm the package is directly selected and identify the first SDK-owned dependency edge.
3. Check the advisory's patched-version guidance, update the coordinated dependency set if appropriate, and rerun the affected restore, AoT, and FullFramework legs.
4. Verify whether the closed historical issue #56981 was closed by a fix that is absent from this tested tree.

This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. ASP.NET Core Identity scaffolding templates use the request-supplied email instead of the account's stored email for password-reset and confirmation messages. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/Scaffolding/issues/3959 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.1 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-640 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Any supported OS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages Updating scaffolding packages/tools does not repair previously generated application code. Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc contains the affected templates. Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design is a parent package that brings in the MVC generator through a minimum-version dependency. For Design, applicability depends on the resolved MVC generator: a project that independently resolves a fixed MVC version does not become vulnerable merely because it retains an older Design reference. ### 8.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.23 | 8.0.24 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.23 | 8.0.24 ### 9.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.12 | 9.0.13 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.12 | 9.0.13 ### 10.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.2 | 10.0.3 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.2 | 10.0.3 ### Additional known affected scaffolding prereleases These are exact known affected versions, not continuous prerelease intervals. Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.3.0 Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet has been incorporated into Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold. Version 20.3.0 supports .NET 8, 9, 10 and 11. Install it as a .NET tool, not as a project package reference. The MVC and Design project packages use the separate fixed versions listed above; 20.3.0 is not a version of those packages. ### Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.x Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold) | >= 20.0.0-preview.1.26156.3, <= 20.1.0 | 20.3.0 The 20.x tool contains the vulnerable Identity and Blazor templates for .NET 8.0 through 11.0. ### Affected legacy prereleases The following exact versions also contain affected templates: - [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) and [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design): `11.0.0-preview.1.26156.3` and `11.0.0-preview.1.26230.3`. - [Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet): `10.0.0-rc.1.25458.5` and `10.0.0-rc.1.25468.1`. Apply the generated-code repair below to applications created with these versions. For new scaffolding, use the Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.3.0 tool, which supports .NET 8 through 11. Migrating to that tool is not an update to an MVC or Design project package reference and does not repair previously generated code. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Check both the installed scaffolding package/tool version and the code it generated. Applications generated with an affected template remain affected after the tool is updated unless their handlers are corrected. The `dotnet-aspnet-codegenerator` command loads generators from the application's dependencies. Check the project's Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design and Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc references against the versions above; updating only the command-line tool does not replace those project dependencies. For applications created with `dotnet new`, check the selected SDK with `dotnet --version` in the working directory. Use `dotnet new list` to identify available templates and `dotnet new uninstall` without arguments to list separately installed template packages. Web ProjectTemplates can be bundled with an SDK or installed separately; a project package reference alone does not identify which template generated the application. ### How do I fix the issue? Update affected scaffolding packages/tools and project dependencies to the patched versions above before generating additional code. Updating scaffolding packages/tools does not repair previously generated applications. Change generated ForgotPassword and ResendEmailConfirmation handlers, including Blazor equivalents, to send only to the stored email returned for the located user; reject missing stored addresses, rebuild and redeploy affected apps. For an existing global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold installation, update the tool: ```shell dotnet tool update --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold --version 20.3.0 ``` For Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet installations, uninstall the old tool and install its replacement: ```shell dotnet tool uninstall --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet dotnet tool install --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold --version 20.3.0 ``` For a new installation, use the install command alone. For local tools, use `--local` instead of `--global` and run the commands from the directory containing the tool manifest. Visual Studio installs and uses the updated scaffolding tool automatically; command-line installations must be updated separately. Visual Studio 17.14 uses the legacy CodeGeneration packages listed above; keep Visual Studio updated and check independently maintained project dependencies. For SDK-bundled templates, install and select an updated SDK that includes the corrected ProjectTemplates version; check `global.json` if an older SDK remains selected. Update separately installed template packs independently. Updating the SDK does not necessarily replace a separately installed template pack. For the affected legacy prereleases, correct the generated handlers before using or deploying the generated application. #### Manual repair for generated Identity handlers This repair also applies to applications generated with the affected 11.0 scaffolding packages and Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet 10.0 RC versions above; it does not require migrating to a different scaffolding tool. In the generated `ForgotPassword` and `ResendEmailConfirmation` handlers, retain the existing user lookup, missing-user responses, password-reset confirmation checks, token generation and callback-URL encoding. After those user checks, retrieve the email from the located account before sending: ```csharp var storedEmail = await UserManager.GetEmailAsync(user); if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(storedEmail)) { throw new InvalidOperationException("Users must have an email."); } ``` In Razor Pages handlers, use `_userManager` instead of `UserManager`. Replace only the recipient argument `Input.Email` with `storedEmail` in `_emailSender.SendEmailAsync`, `EmailSender.SendPasswordResetLinkAsync` and `EmailSender.SendConfirmationLinkAsync`, as applicable. Keep `Input.Email` for the account lookup; do not use it as the message recipient. Apply the change to both handlers, including their Blazor equivalents, then rebuild and redeploy. Reapply the repair if affected templates generate the handlers again. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/Scaffolding. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Check the application's Microsoft.AspNetCore.WebUtilities package reference against the affected range above, including transitive dependencies brought in by Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http. Use `dotnet list package --include-transitive` to inspect resolved dependencies. ### How do I fix the issue? Update each applicable package reference to its patched version listed above, then rebuild and redeploy the application. Updating only the installed runtime does not update an application's standalone package references. Applications referencing Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http must resolve Microsoft.AspNetCore.WebUtilities to version 2.3.14 or later. Add or update a direct WebUtilities reference if necessary to override an older transitive dependency. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in the Aspire CLI. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. An insecure temporary directory used by Aspire CLI-generated builds can allow a local attacker to influence MSBuild response-file discovery and execute code with the privileges of the developer running the CLI. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/issues/22101 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.3 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-379 (Creation of Temporary File in Directory with Insecure Permissions) - **MSRC severity:** Important ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages ### Standalone Aspire CLI Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Aspire.Cli](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli) | >= 13.2.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-arm64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-musl-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-musl-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.osx-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.osx-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.osx-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.osx-arm64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 ### Aspire CLI npm packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [@microsoft/aspire-cli](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-arm64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-arm64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-musl-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-musl-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-arm64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-arm64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 The affected scenario concerns CLI-generated server and integration builds on non-Windows systems when a local attacker can influence automatic MSBuild response-file discovery through an attacker-writable directory. This includes builds started by `aspire sdk generate`, `aspire sdk dump`, and `aspire sdk export`. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? The reported scenario involves a local attacker influencing a generated build through a shared temporary-directory ancestor while another user invokes the Aspire CLI. Versions 13.2.0 through 13.6.4 are affected. Aspire ships independently of .NET. Installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not establish that the affected Aspire CLI has been updated. ### How do I fix the issue? Update the Aspire CLI to version 13.6.5 or later. If installed as a .NET tool, update the Aspire.Cli package. If installed using npm, update @microsoft/aspire-cli to version 13.6.5 or later; its platform-specific dependency must also resolve to version 13.6.5 or later. Otherwise update the CLI through its installation method. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue in the [Aspire repository](https://github.com/microsoft/aspire). ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-120006 - Aspire Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Aspire. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Disclosure of an Aspire Dashboard authentication cookie to a linked service can allow an attacker-controlled container to replay the authenticated session and execute code as the host developer. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/issues/22092 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-201 (Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** macOS - **Architectures:** x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages ### Standalone Aspire Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Aspire.Hosting.AppHost](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Hosting.AppHost) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Hosting](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Hosting) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 The affected scenario involves a Dashboard-authenticated AppHost workflow with an attacker-controlled container and a linked HTTPS YARP gateway. The affected hosting code is in `Aspire.Hosting`, a dependency of `Aspire.Hosting.AppHost`. `Aspire.AppHost.Sdk` supplies the AppHost package implicitly unless the project overrides the default references. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? The reported scenario involves a developer starting an Aspire AppHost, authenticating to its Dashboard, and following a resource link that routes to an attacker-controlled container. All released versions through 13.6.4 are affected. Aspire ships independently of .NET. Installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not establish that the affected Aspire components have been updated. ### How do I fix the issue? Update the AppHost project's `Aspire.Hosting.AppHost` package reference to version 13.6.5 or later. If the project obtains this package implicitly through `Aspire.AppHost.Sdk`, update that SDK reference to version 13.6.5 or later. Explicit package references or central version pins must also resolve `Aspire.Hosting` to version 13.6.5 or later. Restore dependencies, rebuild, and restart the AppHost after updating. Updating only the .NET runtime, .NET SDK, Aspire CLI, or standalone Dashboard does not replace the AppHost project's hosting dependencies. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue in the [Aspire repository](https://github.com/microsoft/aspire). ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-120006](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-120006) ### Acknowledgements - samthewhitehat ### Revisions V1.0 (November 10, 2026): Advisory published.

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-114155 - .NET Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in the .NET SDK's dotnet-watch component. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected SDK installations. A local attacker who can replace or modify a temporary solution file used by dotnet-watch can alter a subsequent build. The fix stores generated solution files in a private temporary directory and keeps each file open with read-only sharing while the build uses it. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/57040 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-367 - **MSRC severity:** Important - **Impact:** Elevation of Privilege ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux, macOS. - **Architectures:** Linux: Arm, Arm64, x64; macOS: Arm64, x64 Windows is outside this advisory's affected scope when its temporary directory is private to the current user, as assumed by the implementation. Shared or insecurely configured Windows temporary directories are not covered by that assumption. ## Affected Packages The .NET SDK includes dotnet-watch and the Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch assembly. Each SDK feature band is a separate servicing line. Update an affected 10.0.3xx installation to the fixed 10.0.4xx SDK listed below. ### .NET SDK 10.0.3xx Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [.NET SDK (dotnet-watch) 10.0.3xx](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/10.0) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.303 | 10.0.404 ### .NET SDK 10.0.4xx Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [.NET SDK (dotnet-watch) 10.0.4xx](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/10.0) | >= 10.0.400, <= 10.0.403 | 10.0.404 ### .NET SDK 11.0.1xx Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [.NET SDK (dotnet-watch) 11.0.1xx](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0) | >= 11.0.100-preview.3.26207.106, <= 11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148 | 11.0.100 ### Separately restored Aspire watch tool Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.303 | 10.0.404 [Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire) | >= 10.0.400, <= 10.0.403 | 10.0.404 [Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire) | >= 11.0.100-preview.3.26207.106, <= 11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148 | 11.0.100 This tool has its own copy of the watch implementation. Updating the SDK does not necessarily replace a separately restored tool. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Run `dotnet --version` from the directory where you run dotnet-watch to identify the selected SDK. Use `dotnet --info` and `dotnet --list-sdks` to check its installation path, OS, architecture, and other installed SDKs. Check the nearest applicable `global.json`, including its `version` and `rollForward` settings: installing a newer SDK does not necessarily change the SDK selected for a pinned project. See [.NET SDK selection](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/versions/selection). Review use of dotnet-watch against the affected intervals above. Membership in a listed feature band alone does not establish that a specific SDK version is vulnerable. For Aspire or other tooling that separately restores Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire, check the actual restored package version separately from the selected SDK. ### How do I fix the issue? The fixed SDK versions are 10.0.404 and 11.0.100, as applicable. Update each affected SDK installation and restart dotnet-watch. For SDKs installed through Visual Studio, update Visual Studio to a release that includes a fixed SDK. Updating only an application runtime does not replace SDK-bundled tools. Ensure that `global.json` and its SDK roll-forward policy select a fixed SDK, then rerun `dotnet --version` in the working directory to verify the selection. The SDK-bundled watch tool is installed beneath that selected SDK's `DotnetTools/dotnet-watch` directory. If Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire is restored separately, update its package reference or the consuming tool's version configuration to 10.0.404 or 11.0.100, as applicable, restore the tool, and restart the consuming process. An SDK update alone does not update that restored copy. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-114155](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-114155) ### Acknowledgements - [Ky0toFu](https://x.com/ky0tofu) ### Revisions V1.0 (November 10, 2026): Advisory published.

Each advisory below remains the authoritative source for its affected versions and remediation. The fixes and required actions differ by CVE; a runtime or SDK update does not replace every standalone package or repair every application. **Feedback:** [Use the shared .NET Runtime feedback thread](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/137280). Please include the CVE number in your question. **Announcement:** [November 2026 .NET Runtime security updates](https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/498). Original CVE-2026-118746 advisory details (preserved) ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Unix Negotiate authentication can accept a request when required channel-binding information is missing. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/137280 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 6.8 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-636 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** Arm, Arm64, x64 ## Affected Packages The tables list affected .NET 11 runtime package versions and fixed versions. The issue occurs during server-side Negotiate authentication with `PolicyEnforcement.Always` when the client omits the channel-binding token. ### .NET 11.0 - Linux runtime packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-arm](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-arm) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-musl-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-musl-arm64) | > 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103, < 11.0.0 | 11.0.0 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-x64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103 | 11.0.0 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-x64) | > 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103, < 11.0.0 | 11.0.0 The six Linux runtime packages at version 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103 reject `PolicyEnforcement.Always` before authentication and are not affected. ### .NET 11.0 - macOS runtime packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.osx-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.osx-arm64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103 | 11.0.0 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.osx-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.osx-x64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103 | 11.0.0 The macOS runtime packages at versions 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103, 11.0.0-rc.1.26425.128, 11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105, and 11.0.0-rc.3.26522.148 reject `PolicyEnforcement.Always` before authentication and are not affected. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Applications using server-side Negotiate authentication with `PolicyEnforcement.Always` are affected when their runtime package version is in the platform-specific ranges above. On Linux, this includes .NET 11 previews 1 through 6 and release candidates 1 through 3. On macOS, this includes .NET 11 previews 1 through 6. Preview 7 is not affected on either platform, and macOS release candidates 1 through 3 are not affected. Self-contained applications include their own runtime; updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace it. ### How do I fix the issue? For affected Linux and macOS .NET 11 prereleases, install .NET 11.0.0 or update each independently referenced runtime package to 11.0.0. Restart applications. Rebuild and redeploy self-contained applications; updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace their embedded runtime. An SDK update alone does not update an application's standalone package references. On macOS, `PolicyEnforcement.Always` remains unsupported and throws `PlatformNotSupportedException`. The update prevents authentication from proceeding without the required protection; it does not add Extended Protection support on macOS. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Issues.Body:
> This issue is a locked mirror of https://github.com/dotnet/core/discussions/10711. See that thread for discussion.

We are pleased to announce the general availability of .NET 11.

Read about the final release in the [.NET Blog announcement](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/announcing-dotnet-11/).

This release includes C# 15, faster developer tools, runtime and library improvements, and new capabilities for web, mobile, desktop, and AI apps. Explore the full release notes below.

## 🛠️ SDK

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/sdk.md)

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/dotnetmaui.md)

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/efcore.md)

## ⏱️ Runtime

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/runtime.md)

## C# 15

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/csharp.md)

## F# 11

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/fsharp.md)

## 🌐 ASP.NET Core & Blazor

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/aspnetcore.md)

## 🖥️ Windows Forms

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/winforms.md)

## 🖥️ Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF)

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/wpf.md)

## 🚀 Get started

To get started with .NET 11, [install the .NET 11 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0).

If you're on Windows using Visual Studio, use an up-to-date [Visual Studio 2026](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/vs/) installation that supports .NET 11.

You can also use Visual Studio Code and the [C# Dev Kit](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-dotnettools.csdevkit) extension with .NET 11.

Before upgrading an existing application, review the [breaking changes in .NET 11](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/compatibility/11), update your target frameworks and dependencies, and run your tests.

Celebrate the release of .NET 11 at [.NET Conf 2026](https://dot.net/conf), November 10-13.

## 🔔 Stay up-to-date with .NET 11

You can stay up-to-date with all the features of .NET 11 with:

* [What's new in Windows Forms](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/desktop/winforms/whats-new/net110)
* [What's new in WPF](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/desktop/wpf/whats-new/net110)
* [Breaking changes in .NET 11](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/compatibility/11)
* [.NET 11 releases](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/README.md)

Be sure to subscribe to the GitHub Discussions [RSS news feed](https://github.com/dotnet/core/discussions/categories/news.atom) for all release announcements.

Issues.Title: .NET October 2026 out-of-band security updates
Issues.Body:
On October 25, 2026, we released out-of-band security updates for .NET 8.0.33, .NET 9.0.22, .NET 10.0.14, and .NET 11 Release Candidate 3 (prerelease). We recommend updating affected applications and build environments as soon as possible. .NET Framework is not affected.

## Release Notes

* [Release details and feedback](https://github.com/dotnet/core/issues/10660)
* [.NET 8.0.33 and .NET SDK 8.0.133 / 8.0.427](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.33/8.0.33.md) ([Download](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0))
* [.NET 9.0.22 and .NET SDK 9.0.123 / 9.0.320](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.22/9.0.22.md) ([Download](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/9.0))
* [.NET 10.0.14 and .NET SDK 10.0.114 / 10.0.403](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.14/10.0.14.md) ([Download](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/10.0))
* [.NET 11.0.0-rc.3.26522.148 and .NET SDK 11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148 (prerelease)](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc3/11.0.0-rc.3.md) ([Download](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0))

## Security advisories

| Advisory | Applicability | Announcement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [CVE-2026-111497](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-p3jp-9v83-76w9) | Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write; all platforms when processing untrusted Brotli data. | [Announcement](https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/494) |
| [CVE-2026-114148](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-r6pf-x897-gm86) | Linux archive ownership; distribution-specific ASP.NET Core archives and source-build engineering inputs. | [Announcement](https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/495) |
| [CVE-2026-70197](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-4mpw-cpwj-hxxj) | Windows sockets memory corruption; corrected October 13 fix. | [Announcement](https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/493) |
| [CVE-2026-102870](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-g27p-qf6j-c96c) | Standalone Blazor WebAssembly debugger packages on .NET 10/11; corrected October 13 fix. | [Announcement](https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/492) |

The October 13 updates did not fully address CVE-2026-70197 and CVE-2026-102870. These out-of-band updates provide the corrected fixes; the original advisory identities and revision history are preserved. For CVE-2026-102870, update the affected standalone Server/DevServer package references; updating only the shared runtime is not a substitute.

For CVE-2026-114148, affected Microsoft-published .NET 8/9 ASP.NET Core runtime and targeting-pack tarball installations require a clean replacement following the advisory. Source-built archives are build/engineering inputs, not directly deployed production runtimes. Update those inputs and recreate their extracted workspaces using ownership-controlled extraction; review and rebuild affected downstream outputs as needed. .NET 10/11 applicability is limited to source-built distributions.

Also announced at [.NET October 2026 Out-of-Band Security Updates](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/dotnet-october-2026-oob-security-updates/).

Please use the [release feedback issue](https://github.com/dotnet/core/issues/10660) for release-wide issues and the linked per-CVE discussions for advisory questions.
